open_for_the_seal: Criterion 5's first half is predicted to FAIL (prediction 4). Free-page reporting returns freed anonymous memory, but a heavy command's growth here is mostly page cache (guest and host-side), which it never returns. Options: keep the bar as sealed above and let the rungs record the miss (recommended; the spec's wording is 'falls back toward its working set'), or decide now that cache counts as working set and judge only anonymous memory, which needs a guest reading the analysis does not have.

Design input, whatever the verdict: for a lease's charge to follow its working set, something must drop the guest's clean page cache on idle (e.g. drop_caches or a balloon inflate before reporting) and the workspace image's host cache must not stay charged to the VM's cgroup.
py_import's calibrated gain (0.39 probes, 0.47 seeded on 4 warm calls) sits close to the 0.30 bar; N=128 contention could push it under.
Criterion 5's second-half bar (1.5x) is new, set here between the host-page-cache case (~1x) and E17a's cold case (~5x).

The 256 MiB stages (ram256-*: pycache-d64 N=1 both arms, the squeeze-256 baselines, climb and sbx rung) cannot measure what they were for: py_analyze is OOM-killed in a 256 MiB guest in BOTH arms (calibration.smoke_256), so every heavy turn fails, criterion 5's d64 reading has no heavy Exec, and a squeeze-256 climb stops on failed calls, not on memory. Options: (a) cut the ram256 stages from E17b and record the limit (recommended: they are reported-only, criteria 1-5 do not depend on them, saves ~3 rig h); (b) run them as is and report the OOMs; (c) build a 256-specific library with a smaller py_analyze (new workload + calibration, ~half a day).
sealNote: Sealed on the user's go-ahead (2026-11-17, 'go ahead with the recommendation'), before any measured E17b rung. Decisions at the seal: (1) criterion 5's first-half bar stays as written (criterion5_thresholds) and the rungs record the predicted miss; cache is not counted as working set. (2) The second-half bar is 1.5x sbx's median py_grep. (3) The ram256 stages are cut (ruling E17B-R45: needs kind ram256, run only with E17B_RAM256=1); pycache-d64 is not measured, and verdict.py's reported d64 reading stays empty. (4) Predictions 1-10 as drafted. The optional ship-30/ship-120 default ladders stay off (E17B_OPTIONAL unset) unless the user asks.

deviations.why: footprint-drift repeats roughly double rung time; saves ~8-9 rig hours so criterion 1 lands on 2026-11-18 for the v0.11.0 release; risk: a regression at the new pin below the start N goes unseen

deviations.why: a rig error, not a measurement change; without it the climb and the N=128 pycache rungs cannot run on this host

deviations.what: lease ends caused by the driver's end-of-run cut are excluded from criterion 4 like live_at_stop and ended_after_sweep (ended_by_run_cut: an unmatched end whose key's last call is cut_at_end, at or after its send second); the cut call itself is tagged cut_at_end, not unknown, in the warm/cold join

All 3 agent_dead ends of E17b lie within 1 s of their worker's stop; none mid-run

deviations.what: the 500000-file ownership walk is not measured: its 4096 MiB workspace cannot be mounted by a guest restored from a snapshot whose workspace drive is 2 GiB (moca deploy/microvm/build-snapshot.sh WORKSPACE_IMAGE_BYTES is fixed at 2 GiB; the worker's startup probe fails 'mount /workspace exited 32' and the worker never attaches); prediction 9 is judged at 10000 and 100000 files
